title: Zuri and the Footprints After Rain
subtitle: A Copper Tree story and colouring adventure

pages.heading: Something in the Mud
pages.text:
Rain had washed Copper Tree clean. Outside the Lookout, the friends' garden clubhouse, Zuri spotted muddy marks beside an overturned flowerpot.
“Footprints!” she whispered.
Tayo peered over her shoulder. “Something has landed.”
“Something with paws,” said Zuri.
Under the bench, Crumpet the neighbourhood cat opened one eye.
Zuri pointed. “And there is our suspect.”
pages.activity: Draw a garden after rain. Include three things you might notice on a rainy morning.
pages.art_brief: Zuri crouches beside muddy marks and an overturned empty pot outside the small Lookout shed. Tayo peers over her shoulder. Cat under nearby bench. Broad open colouring areas.

pages.heading: The First Guess
pages.text:
Crumpet stretched, yawned and sat on Amara's sketchbook.
“He looks guilty,” said Eli.
“He looks comfortable,” said Nia.
Zuri drew a cat beside the footprints. Then she added a large tick.
Kofi adjusted his glasses. “Did anyone see him make them?”
Zuri's pencil stopped.
“Well, no. But he is right here.”
“So are we,” said Nia.
pages.activity: Draw your first guess about the visitor. Leave room beside it for another idea.
pages.art_brief: Crumpet sitting on closed sketchbook, Zuri holding notebook, Nia and Eli nearby. Emphasise amused faces. No exact track puzzle.

pages.heading: Following Carefully
pages.text:
Mrs Bennett was sweeping the garden path.
“May we follow the marks?” Zuri asked.
“Along the paths, with me,” she said. “Leave the beds to the plants.”
The prints crossed a patch of mud and stopped at the gravel.
“The creature vanished!” said Tayo.
“Or walked somewhere that leaves fewer marks,” said Kofi.
They all looked at the gravel.
pages.activity: Draw garden beds with a path between them. Keep your route around the plants.
pages.art_brief: Mrs Bennett and Zuri at garden path where mud meets gravel. Raised beds, clear accessible paths, large leaves. Adult is practical older Black woman with short natural grey hair, simple cardigan and trousers.

pages.heading: A Gap in the Hedge
pages.text:
Beyond the gravel, Nia noticed another muddy patch beside a gap beneath the hedge.
“There are more over here.”
Zuri leaned forward, then stopped at the path's edge.
“Perhaps Crumpet went through.”
“Perhaps,” Mrs Bennett agreed. “We can look from here.”
Amara sketched the gap.
Eli held her pencil case. For once, he managed to stand completely still.
pages.activity: Draw a leafy hedge. Invent a tiny creature that could shelter underneath it.
pages.art_brief: Nia pointing from path towards hedge gap. Amara sketching with Eli holding pencil case. Hedge and muddy patch remain distant, children do not crawl through.

pages.heading: A Very Unhelpful Cat
pages.text:
They returned to find Crumpet asleep on Zuri's notebook.
“He has eaten the evidence,” Tayo announced.
“He is sitting on it,” said Amara.
Zuri gently slid the notebook free. Her large tick stared back at her.
Below it, she wrote a question mark.
“I still think it might be Crumpet,” she said. “But thinking isn't the same as seeing.”
pages.activity: Draw something funny Crumpet might choose as a bed. Give Zuri a new question to investigate.
pages.art_brief: Zuri retrieves notebook from relaxed cat on bench. Tayo theatrical and Amara amused. Notebook blank for layout to handle symbols.

pages.heading: The Garden Camera
pages.text:
“There might be a way to look back,” said Mrs Bennett.
She showed them the little wildlife camera facing the hedge. She used it to see which animals visited after dark.
“Can it see yesterday?” asked Tayo.
“If it recorded something.”
Mrs Bennett fetched her tablet. The six friends gathered beside her.
Zuri held her notebook open at a fresh page.
pages.activity: Design a cover for the crew’s garden wildlife notebook. Draw an animal you would like to learn about.
pages.art_brief: Mrs Bennett showing six children a small tablet near bench. Wildlife camera mounted facing hedge, clear indication garden wildlife use. Simple composition with space.

pages.heading: Wait for the Visitor
pages.text:
On the screen, the garden was grey and quiet.
A leaf fluttered. Rain splashed. Nothing happened.
“Excellent film about a leaf,” Eli whispered.
Then a pointed nose appeared beneath the hedge.
Two ears followed. A narrow body slipped through, then a long, bushy tail.
“A fox!” Zuri breathed.
Everybody leaned closer. Mrs Bennett paused the recording so everyone could see.
pages.activity: Draw the visitor appearing from behind a leaf. What would you notice first?
pages.art_brief: Tablet close view held by adult with recorded fox emerging under hedge; Zuri and Eli watching. Clear tablet frame distinguishes recording from live animal. No tiny UI text.

pages.heading: Across the Mud
pages.text:
Mrs Bennett played the next part. The fox stepped across the muddy patch, passed over the gravel and walked beside the flowerpot.
Its flank brushed the pot. Over it went.
“There!” cried Zuri. “We can see it happening!”
The fox trotted away.
Crumpet padded into the garden much later. He walked straight to the bench and curled up.
pages.activity: Draw the fox’s journey through the garden. What happens at the end?
pages.art_brief: Three roomy sequential vignettes inside screen border: fox crossing mud, brushing empty pot which tips, fox leaving. Fox four legs and bushy tail. No children interacting with fox.

pages.heading: A Better Answer
pages.text:
Zuri looked at her cat drawing.
“I was wrong about Crumpet.”
“And you found out,” said Kofi.
Zuri rubbed out the tick and drew a fox beside the cat.
Amara passed her an orange pencil. “A new clue deserves a new picture.”
Underneath, Zuri wrote, “The camera showed a fox making the trail.”
That felt better than being certain.
pages.activity: Draw Zuri’s new answer beside a picture of her first guess. Tell someone what helped her change her mind.
pages.art_brief: Zuri seated with notebook drawing fox, Kofi beside her, Amara offers pencil. Warm expressive concentration, no embedded text.

pages.heading: Room for Visitors
pages.text:
Mrs Bennett stood the empty pot upright and moved it away from the narrow path.
“We can give our visitors room,” said Nia.
They left the hedge gap clear and made a wildlife page for the Lookout.
“Shall we invite the fox inside?” asked Tayo.
“Outside is its place,” said Mrs Bennett.
“Crumpet hasn't read that rule,” said Eli.
pages.activity: Design a wildlife page with room for drawings of garden visitors. Add a quiet place to watch from.
pages.art_brief: Nia and Mrs Bennett relocating empty pot onto shelf while remaining children make simple wildlife poster at outdoor table. Hedge gap unobstructed.

pages.heading: The Next Morning
pages.text:
The next morning, Zuri arrived with her notebook. Fresh marks dotted the damp path.
“Another fox?” asked Eli.
“Maybe,” said Zuri, smiling. “Let's see what we can find out.”
Mrs Bennett raised one muddy boot.
“Would this help?”
The friends burst out laughing.
Zuri drew a boot on her page. Her notebook had room for all sorts of answers.
pages.activity: Invent a funny boot-sole pattern. Draw the trail it could leave across your page.
pages.art_brief: Mrs Bennett raises one boot revealing simple sole while Zuri and Eli laugh. Clearly oversized human boot marks on path. Keep boot and tracks broadly illustrative.

pages.heading: The Question Shelf
pages.text:
Inside the Lookout, the friends added their wildlife notebook to the discovery shelf.
Zuri wrote a message on the first page. “Look closely. Ask questions. Leave room for surprises.”
Crumpet jumped onto the empty chair beside her.
“I know what you are doing,” she told him.
He curled up and closed his eyes.
This time, Zuri had seen it for herself.
pages.activity: Draw yourself visiting the Lookout. What question would you add to the wildlife notebook?
pages.art_brief: Lookout interior with Zuri writing notebook, Crumpet on chair, other friends nearby and discovery shelf. Empty drawing space lets reader add themselves. Warm ending, uncluttered colouring shapes.

Mrs Bennett seated on bench holds a tablet while Zuri and Kofi watch. Crumpet curls up beside Zuri’s notebook. Small wildlife camera on post aimed towards hedge in background. Warm curious faces, simple composition.

Zuri draws a fox in an open notebook at outdoor table, Amara offers her a pencil and Nia helps Mrs Bennett move an empty flowerpot onto a low shelf in background. Hedge gap stays open. Simplify to generous colouring areas, no lettering.
